lesson_title: Take Away the Whole Bag: The Minus Before a Bracket
hook_text: Minus a bracket. Half the class flips one sign and moves on. Here is the bag that shows why every sign flips.
clip_script: A bracket is a bag. Minus a bracket means take away the whole bag — everything in it. The bag holds x squared, plus 4x, minus 1. Take it away: minus x squared, minus 4x, PLUS 1. Every sign flips, because you cannot remove a bag and leave half the contents behind. Now sort the fruit: 3x squared minus x squared is 2x squared; minus 2x minus 4x is minus 6x; 5 plus 1 is 6. Not sure? Plug in x equals 1. Original: 6 take away 4 is 2. Your answer: 2 minus 6 plus 6 is 2. Match. Flip only the first sign and you get 8 — busted. And multiplying monomials: numbers times, little numbers add. 3x squared times 4x cubed is 12x to the fifth. Bag, fruit, check.
visual_style: A paper bag labelled with the bracket is lifted off a whiteboard and its three terms tumble out with their signs flipping in red; fruit icons sort into piles; a plug-in check ticks green.
pacing: A clear setup, one dramatic flip, a fast sort and a satisfying check.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and never lose a sign to a bracket again.
